extracted.intended_audience: policy makers, IP statisticians, patent/ trademark office staff, researchers and analysts using WIPO statistical indicators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and definitional notes for interpreting WIPO's patent/trademark statistical tables and procedural metrics across national and regional offices. Includes data caveats, metric definitions (e.g., class count, FTE), and comparability notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications by origin data completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Applications by origin data are incomplete, because some offices do not report by origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this caveat when interpreting 'applications by origin' columns — some offices do not report origin breakdowns, so totals or origin-based comparisons may be incomplete or biased.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident-applications-not-reported flag
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) The office did not report resident applications therefore applications by origin data may be incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an office did not report resident applications, origin and resident/non-resident splits for that office are not reliable. Treat such offices' origin breakdowns as incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: OAPI as national office (aggregated reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) The African Intellectual Property Organization (OAPI) acts as the national office for patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OAPI data represent a regional aggregated office acting for member states; interpreting country-level origin or resident counts should account for OAPI's aggregator role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation for missing / not applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: '.. indicates not available. n.a. indicates not applicable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables use '..' for data not available and 'n.a.' for not applicable; respect these markers rather than treating them as zeros when analyzing datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class count (trademark) definition and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Class count: A trademark application can refer to different classes of goods or services. Many offices use the Nice Classification. Applications received at these offices are classified according to one or more of 45 Nice classes. Some offices allow only single-class filing, others permit multi-class filing. To improve international comparison of the number of applications received, it helps to compare class counts across offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing trademark activity across offices, prefer application class counts (number of classes specified) rather than raw application counts because filing systems differ (single-class vs multi-class). Note that WIPO began using this method for cross-office comparison in 2004.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nice Classification (trademark) implication
rubrics_metrics.description: Many offices use the Nice Classification. Applications received at these offices are classified according to one or more of 45 Nice classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses relying on class-level sectoral breakdowns should use the Nice Classification mapping when possible; differences in class usage across offices can affect sectoral comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural metrics: Total applications processed / Granted / Rejected / Withdrawn or abandoned
rubrics_metrics.description: Table columns include 'Total applications processed', 'Granted', 'Rejected', and 'Withdrawn or abandoned'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the core procedural outcome metrics for offices. Be aware procedural definitions differ across offices (see note on 'rejection' below), so cross-office comparisons of these counts should account for local procedural policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection recording differences (procedural caveat)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: For instance, 'rejection' is not recorded as a final decision in Canada, because applicants are informed of the action they must take ... if an applicant cannot provide the required information, they are regarded as having abandoned the application. A similar situation pertains in Australia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume 'rejected' counts are directly comparable across offices: some offices record rejections differently (or record abandonment instead), which affects interpretation of 'rejected' vs 'withdrawn/abandoned' tallies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of examiners (FTE) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of examiners (FTE). Note: FTE is full time equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use FTE to compare examiner capacity across offices rather than raw headcount; FTE normalizes part-time and full-time staffing. Consider this when relating throughput to staff levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: First office action and final office decision (months) as timeliness metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Table columns 'First office action (months)' and 'Final office decision (months)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These temporal metrics measure average or typical processing delays. Procedural and definitional differences across offices can affect these values; harmonize definitions before comparing (e.g., what triggers 'first action' or 'final decision').

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT national phase entry (table column)
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT national phase entry appears as a column in the applications tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This metric captures national/regional entries originating from PCT filings; use it to separate domestically-filed applications from PCT-derived filings in analyses of office workloads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident vs Non-resident breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables present 'Resident' and 'Non-resident' application and grant counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish resident (domestic filers) vs non-resident (foreign filers) when assessing national innovation activity versus inbound filings. Missing resident data (see flags) undermines this breakdown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data provenance and extraction date
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All figures reflect the WIPO Statistics Database as extracted in August 2024. Analysts should record extraction date and be aware later extractions may differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonization recommendation for international comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: When differences between filing systems across national and regional offices are harmonized based on application class count, the 2023 on-year decrease in trademark filing was slightly more pronounced at 2%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international trend analysis, harmonize filing-system differences (e.g., via class counts) to obtain more comparable measures; otherwise raw application counts can mislead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use caution interpreting procedural data across offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Every effort has been made to compile procedural data based on common definitions and concepts, but procedural differences make it extremely difficult to fully harmonize such data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat cross-office procedural comparisons as indicative rather than definitive; document known procedural differences (rejection recording, timing definitions, aggregated regional offices) when reporting comparative analyses.
